second_read.note: Hamiltonian H = J1 Σ si·sj + J2 Σ si·sj over NN and NNN pairs 'counting each bond once', J1 = 1, periodic boundaries; Lanczos ED, deterministic, bound_type exact. Units and J2 label checked inside the paper: E/N = 2⟨s0·s1⟩ + 2 J2 ⟨s0·s6⟩ from Table 2 (R = (1,0) and (1,1)) gives -0.636617, 1.7e-6 from the table value (the correlations are printed to 6 decimals). Cluster: the paper's Fig. 1 (vectors not printed in the text). Reconstructed from the figure's site-label coordinates and its periodic images (labels 3 and 23 repeated at a shift (2,−6), 35 and 38 at (−6,−2)): the tilted square torus T1 = (6,2), T2 = (−2,6), |T|² = 40, orthogonal, all 40 labels distinct modulo T1, T2, no mirror symmetry (point group C4). The paper's GS-sector size, 'nh = 430909650 for N = 40', equals exactly the q = (0,0), C4-irrep A, spin-flip-even dimension of that cluster by the character formula (out/VP10-heisenberg-j1j2/sector_dims.mjs; the other q = 0 sectors have 430693098 (A−), 430909268 (B+), 430693228 (B−)), which confirms the reconstruction and identifies the sector that was diagonalised. The ground state at this J2 is Néel-like or paramagnetic (M²(π,π) ≥ 0.079, M²(π,0) ≤ 0.0145 in Table 1), the regime whose ground state lies in the sector connected to J2 = 0; on the 6 × 6 torus the ground state stays A1 there. Only row on its instance; no duplicate. Independent recompute requested (group VE-exact-recompute has it as todo): cluster T1 = (6,2), T2 = (−2,6), sector q = 0, A, spin flip +.
